Freya.title: Freya: Beauty, Magic and Warrior Power
Freya.description: An evocation of the Norse goddess Freya, blending beauty, magic and warrior power to honor the mythology of Chaco's immigrants.
Freya.history:
The creation of this work is a manifestation of the artist's deep connection with his land and, at the same time, with the cultures that have enriched it. The sculpture is born from the intention to pay homage to the mythologies and beliefs of the immigrants who arrived in the province of Resistencia, Chaco, and who merged with the Creole, Guaraní and Qom cultures.

The artist maintains his characteristic style of using body forms to tell stories. In this piece, the face and expression of the character are key to conveying a narrative. The greatest technical and artistic challenge was to combine feminine beauty with immense power, elements that are the essence of the figure of Freya. The ram horns, the complex hairstyle and the symbology engraved on her skin were carefully chosen to reflect the cultural heritage of Nordic traditions. Through this work, the artist seeks to highlight the blend of beliefs and cultures that have reached his land, turning the figure of the Nordic goddess into a vehicle to explore a unique cultural dialogue. It is a work that not only celebrates the beauty of a deity, but also honors the rich diversity that defines the region.

matero.title: Alma y Mate: Gaucho Tradition and Introspection
matero.description: A tribute to gaucho tradition and introspection, elevating the everyday act of drinking mate to a moment of meditation.
matero.history:
The work Alma y Mate is the result of the artist's fascination with the archetype of the gaucho and his relationship with nature and time. Santiago Guarnieri set out to explore that moment of solitude and peace where mate becomes a faithful companion, a space for personal reflection. Through this piece, he seeks to highlight the figure of the gaucho as a bearer of a legacy of wisdom and work, visible in the marks the sun has left on his skin.

The sculpture transcends mere representation and becomes a symbol of the mate ritual as a moment of introspection and planning before the daily work begins. The waves connecting the character with the mate symbolize the soul of the man who merges with the ritual, turning a simple act into a unique moment of contemplation. Through the meticulousness in the details of the face and beard, the artist not only seeks precision, but also wants to invite the viewer to contemplate the richness of traditions that are part of Argentina's cultural identity.

Escultura-de-San-Martin.title: Busto del General San Martín: Legacy of Firmness and Determination
Escultura-de-San-Martin.description: A tribute to the legacy of José de San Martín, transcending portraiture to study the General's firmness and determination.
Escultura-de-San-Martin.history:
The creation of this work arises from deep admiration for San Martín's role as a military leader and strategist. The artist set himself the challenge of going beyond conventional portraiture, seeking an image that would resonate with popular imagination while being rooted in historical precision. For this, he relied on the 1827 daguerreotype, the most reliable source of his anatomical features, fusing that reality with the hero's mystique.

The research process was as crucial as the artistic one. The artist consulted Argentine Army databases to accurately replicate the embroidery of the gallons and the design of the medals, ensuring that each element was a complete reference to his victories and honors. The sculpture, which lacks an explicit title, seeks to ensure that the viewer is not forced into a single interpretation, allowing the work to 'speak for itself' and for the General's values—such as his commitment, courage and rigor—to be perceived through the contemplation of each detail. The choice of the height, designed for a public space, underscores the intention to keep his legacy alive and serve as a constant reminder of his invaluable contribution to the history of humanity.

Tamborcito-de-Tacuari.title: El Eco de la Infancia: Tribute to Pedro Ríos
Tamborcito-de-Tacuari.description: The work captures the duality of Pedro Ríos, the Drummer of Tacuarí: the innocence of a child and the courage of a hero.
Tamborcito-de-Tacuari.history:
In his work, Santiago Guarnieri presents Pedro Ríos, the Drummer of Tacuarí, not as an idealized historical figure, but as what he was: a child. Guarnieri masterfully captures the duality of his character: the innocence of a child from the shores of the Paraná, mixed with the courage of a hero who faces an overwhelming destiny. The sculpture immortalizes the exact moment when Pedro receives the elements that will accompany him in his feat: a drum and a leather strap, symbols of his commitment and sacrifice.

The expression of the face is one of deep courage and fear of the unknown, that of someone who, despite his young age, decides to move forward for ideals he may not fully understand, but which resonate in his heart. The skin, smooth and unblemished, contrasts with the hardness of the artist's previous works and highlights the youth of the character, accentuating the tragedy of a childhood sacrificed for the sake of the homeland.

History of the Work: The Silence of the Drum
Pedro Ríos integrates perfectly into Guarnieri's narrative about regional and national identity. If San Fernando Rey explored European heritage and Monte Quemado addressed the fragility of indigenous peoples, this work pays tribute to a regional hero, a child who, born in the deepest part of the Argentine littoral, becomes a symbol of dedication and love for the homeland. It is a reminder that the identity of a nation is built not only with great figures, but also with the sacrifice of those who, like Pedro Ríos, decide to fight for their land.

Unlike his previous works, Guarnieri experiments in this piece with new materials: clay is used as a means to an end, which is resin and fiberglass. These materials allow him to capture with unusual precision even the smallest detail of the figure, giving it a smooth and delicate finish that underscores the child's fragility, but also the strength of his spirit.

Napalpi.title: Napalpí: A Tribute to Chaco Resistance
Napalpi.description: A moving tribute to the victims of the 1924 massacre in Chaco, giving a human face to pain and resistance.
Napalpi.history:
The Napalpí sculpture is a moving tribute to the victims and survivors of the 1924 massacre in the Chaco province. Through the figure of a fictional chief, the work seeks to give a human face to pain and resistance. The character's face, furrowed by wrinkles that speak of a life of wisdom and suffering, reflects the unimaginable cruelty that humans can inflict, but also the resistance to oblivion.

The chief's gaze, directed towards the sky, evokes the moment when an Argentine Army plane, on its baptismal flight, was used to distract the children before the attack. The piece stands on a carved cedar base, which seeks to represent the roots of those who lost their lives, while the thin and curved connection between the head and the base symbolizes the fragility of life and the work's desire to rise. The details of his headdress and necklace, made with materials that refer to Qom and Wichi crafts, reinforce the identity of a people and their deep sense of belonging to the land.

The creation of Napalpí is the artist's response to the need to keep the history of his province alive. For Santiago Guarnieri, art has the responsibility to be a vehicle for memory, especially when historical records are scarce. The artist, a native of Chaco, assumes the commitment to tell the history of his people, understanding that being a young province, there is still much to be told to strengthen its identity.

The choice of clay as the main material is not accidental: it represents the mud and earth from which we come, a noble material that, when transformed into ceramic by fire, symbolizes the resilience of a people. The modeling and carving process was a way to pay homage, to give life and dignity to a story that deserves to be heard. Through this work, the artist invites us to empathy and reflection.
Napalpi.materials: Ceramic and cedar wood sculpture (40 cm tall)

San-Fernando-Rey.title: San Fernando Rey: A Face Before Infinity
San-Fernando-Rey.description: A representation of Resistencia's patron saint stripped of his majesty, revealing the introspection of a man in the twilight of his life.
San-Fernando-Rey.history:
In this work, Santiago Guarnieri presents a King Saint Ferdinand stripped of conventional majesty, revealing instead the introspection of a man in the twilight of his life. The sculpture, with a cobalt patina that gives it a timeless quality, seems extracted from an ancient story, raw and unadorned. Guarnieri masterfully combines the nobility of the character with a vulnerability that resonates deeply.

The artist chooses San Fernando Rey, patron of his city, Resistencia, to explore the identity forged by stories and beliefs from other lands. The expression on the king's face is not of victory, but of serene melancholy. It is the countenance of someone who has known power and battle, but now, stripped of his armor, faces the fragility of his own body and the equality of death.

The crown, far from being a luxury object, is simple and austere, with the mark of the hammer that forged it, symbolizing the values of Catholicism that the king embraced. The crosses that crown it reaffirm his faith and devotion. The mantle, which looks like a bed before death, wraps a body worn by time and battles, exposing the man beneath the monarch.

Guarnieri's technique, which combines polished and rough textures, gives the work a unique personality. The cobalt oxide sphere on which the king rests represents infinity and the constant cycle of the universe, a visual echo of the work's central message. With his gaze towards the horizon, San Fernando invites us to a moment of reflection: a final balance of achievements and failures, faith and humility coexisting in a single figure, who in the end, meets the purest fragility.

History of the work: The Stripped King
"San Fernando Rey" is a fundamental piece in Santiago Guarnieri's exploration of identity and historical influences. Often, our own identity is shaped by figures that, although distant in time and space, leave a lasting mark on our culture.
San-Fernando-Rey.materials: Ceramic (39cm tall, 26 cm wide and 19 cm long)
San-Fernando-Rey.technique: Molded and sculpted in clay, hollowed, fired and patinated with cobalt oxide.

Introspeccion.title: Introspección: A Study of Inner Silence
Introspeccion.description: A powerful study of inner silence that invites a pause in a world of constant stimuli.
Introspeccion.history:
The creation of Introspection arises from the need to represent a universal moment of reflection. The artist seeks to capture that instant when a person stops to look within, searching for the answers needed to move forward. Without being the portrait of a particular historical character, this work focuses on the human experience. The artist relies on body language and forms to convey the concerns and feelings that accompany us throughout life.

In a world dominated by technology and constant exposure, this work stands as a counterpoint, a reminder of the importance of finding a moment of personal peace. Through empathy, the piece seeks for the viewer to connect with the character and feel invited to perform their own exercise of introspection. The meticulous work with clay and the interplay of textural contrasts are not just an aesthetic choice; they are a fundamental part of the work's narrative, a visual guide accompanying the viewer on their journey through the layers of meaning underlying the piece.

Plumitas.title: Félix: Qom Serenity and Conviction
Plumitas.description: A tribute to Félix Díaz, Qom activist, capturing the serenity and conviction that ideals can be defended without violence.
Plumitas.history:
The creation of Félix is an extension of Santiago Guarnieri's artistic exploration of the identity and history of the peoples of northern Argentina. Through this piece, he seeks to give face to the leaders who, with their actions, forge the identity of a community. The artist was attracted to the figure of Félix Díaz, a leader who inspires respect for his tenacious and peaceful struggle.

The work is a continuity of the artist's artistic language, in which the body and facial expression become the medium to tell a story. The sculpture's face, with its open eyes and a gaze conveying tranquility, opposes the marks life has left on his skin. The contrast in texture, between the smooth skin and the rough wooden base, symbolizes the coexistence of fragility and strength. Ultimately, Félix is not just a portrait; it is a testimony of struggle, a call to reflection on the importance of peace and a celebration of a leader's deep connection with the land of his ancestors.
Plumitas.materials: Clay and wood sculpture (25 cm tall)

sombrerito.title: Esperanza: The Face of Effort and Honesty
sombrerito.description: An archetype of the anonymous rural worker, whose expression of hope and weathered face tell a story of effort and honesty.
sombrerito.history:
In this work called "Hope", Santiago Guarnieri presents a figure that, despite its apparent simplicity, encapsulates the essence of the Argentine countryman. It is not a portrait of a person, but of an archetype: the anonymous rural worker, whose hands and face tell a story of effort and honesty. Guarnieri has sculpted in clay the fundamental values of life on the plains: humility, simplicity and a deep connection with the land.

The expression on his face is the key to the work. With his gaze directed toward the sky, he conveys a mix of experience and hope. The wrinkles and furrows in the skin are not only the result of the passage of time and the sun; they are the marks of wisdom forged in daily work. Through modeling and sculpting in clay, the artist achieves a texture that speaks to us of the hardness of a life dedicated to the field, but at the same time highlights an inner light, an unwavering faith in a better future. The chromatic contrast, intentionally minimized, serves so that the shape of the face, its pose and its expression, are the true protagonists.

History of the Work: The Face of the Nation
This sculpture is part of Santiago Guarnieri's series of works on Chaco identity. While each piece addresses a different aspect, all converge on the idea that the identity of a region is built from a rich diversity of stories and characters. If "San Fernando Rey" explored European heritage and "Monte Quemado" made visible the tragedy of indigenous peoples, this work pays tribute to the men and women who, with their work, forge the nation day by day.

Through this bust, Guarnieri brings to the fore those who often remain in the shadows. It is a tribute to the silent and vital labor of those who till the land and sustain life.

Cicatrices-del-Alma.title: Cicatrices del Alma: A Journey of Resilience
Cicatrices-del-Alma.description: A male torso that symbolizes how emotional wounds become part of identity, a sign of healing and strength.
Cicatrices-del-Alma.history:
In his work "Scars of the Soul", Santiago Guarnieri presents a figure that delves into the vulnerability and strength of the human spirit. The sculpture, a male torso with a finish that combines smooth and rough textures, symbolizes the complexity of personal experience. The incomplete figure and the tearing of the skin suggest emotional and physical wounds, which form an integral part of the individual's identity.

The work invites the viewer to deep introspection. The scars are not only a sign of pain, but also of healing and personal growth. The serene expression of the face, with a slight tilt and closed eyes, evokes a state of inner peace and acceptance, a stillness reached through resilience in the face of suffering. The technique, combining clay modeling with resin casting and a gold and pastel patina finish, highlights the duality of the work: the fragility of being and the richness of the experiences that have marked it.

History of the Work: From Vulnerability to Strength
"Scars of the Soul" marks a new chapter in Guarnieri's exploration of human identity. Unlike the figures in his previous works, which focus on regional and national identity through archetypal or historical characters, this piece is an immersion into a universal and timeless concept: the human condition. The work reminds us that our difficulties and wounds are an essential part of our personal journey and contribute to our strength. Through this fragmented torso, Guarnieri proposes a powerful reflection on how pain does not define us, but transforms us, leaving a golden trace within us. It is a work that invites us to see our own scars not as weaknesses, but as symbols of our capacity to heal and move forward.
Cicatrices-del-Alma.materials: Resin with gold patina and pastel colors

Busto-de-San-Martin.title: El Rostro de la Historia: A Tribute to San Martín
Busto-de-San-Martin.description: An intimate and human representation of the Liberator, based on the 1848 daguerreotype.
Busto-de-San-Martin.history:
In this bust of San Martín, sculptor Santiago Guarnieri departs from military and heroic iconography to immerse himself in a more intimate and human representation of the Liberator. The work is a challenge, an attempt to blend the popular image with the only reliable physiognomic reference available: the daguerreotype taken in 1848.

The hero's face, modeled and sculpted in clay, reflects a deep mix of resignation and acceptance. In his gaze one perceives the wisdom of a life dedicated to freedom.

Tiro-al-Blanco.title: Libre: The Fury and Nobility of the Chaco Horse
Tiro-al-Blanco.description: A tribute to the Creole horse of Chaco, capturing its indomitable strength and spirit of freedom in a pose of astonishing vitality.
Tiro-al-Blanco.history:
In the sculpture "Free", Santiago Guarnieri pays tribute to the Creole horse of Chaco, an animal that is both a symbol of indomitable strength and an essential work companion. The work, with its realistic and expressionist style, captures the essence of this animal through a pose of astonishing vitality: with its front legs raised, the horse seems suspended in the air, a gesture evoking the freedom and power of the bush.
The inspiration for the work comes directly from the poet Antonio Falcón, who describes the Chaco horse as a being of light rays entering the bush. The sculpture becomes a tangible manifestation of those verses, capturing the rebellion and beauty of an animal living in communion with its land. The material, modeled and sculpted clay, colored with pigments, gives a rough texture to the piece, a reflection of the roughness of the terrain and the hardness of life in the country.

History of the Work: The Steed of Collective Identity
With "Free", Guarnieri expands his exploration of Chaco identity beyond human figures, integrating a new element: the horse, a protagonist of the region's history and present. If "Hope" represented the values of the rural worker, and "Monte Quemado" denounced environmental devastation, this work celebrates the deep connection between nature and man. The horse is a witness to the daily life of Chaco, carrying teachers and students, pulling carts, and being a symbol of the "nobility of the future".

The title, "Free", synthesizes the essence of the work: a tribute to an untamed being that, despite its service, maintains its wild spirit. The sculpture is a testimony of the bond between the animal and its environment, a reminder that the identity of a region is forged both in the stories of its people and in the majesty of its fauna.
Tiro-al-Blanco.materials: Modeled and sculpted clay, colored with pigments

Fabriziano.title: Legado: Portrait of Serenity and Peace
Fabriziano.description: An intimate and emotional portrait of Fabriciano Gómez, capturing the master with closed eyes, conveying deep serenity and peace.
Fabriziano.history:
The creation of Legacy arises from a personal and deep admiration for the humility and generosity of Fabriciano Gómez. The artist, who had the opportunity to know him and to experience the growth of the Sculpture Biennial of Resistencia, felt the need to pay tribute to this Chaco reference. The artistic challenge was considerable: to convey the character's essence without resorting to communication through gaze, a fundamental characteristic in the artist's work. The solution was to use the gesture of closed eyes to symbolize the serenity with which the master communicated his ideas.

This piece has a specially emotional meaning, as it represents the artist's connection with his own history and with the growth of his city. From childhood, the artist walked the streets of Resistencia, contemplating the works that aroused his curiosity and drove him to question how they were created. The Biennial, promoted by Fabriciano, became a source of answers, a space where sculptors allowed him to understand the creative process. Through meticulous research of the face and realistic finishing technique, the sculpture seeks for the audience to feel the same closeness that the artist felt with the figure of Fabriciano, a man whose sculptural and cultural legacy is cemented in the heart of his beloved city.

Manos.title: Manos: An Anatomical Study
Manos.description: An exploration of form and human emotion, where a simple hand gesture captures a story of intention and desire.
Manos.history:
This sculpture is born from the artist's conviction that anatomical knowledge is fundamental for an authentic representation of human emotion. For Santiago Guarnieri, anatomy is not an end in itself, but a tool to understand how each muscle and each gesture contribute to the narrative of a piece. In this sense, Hands is conceived as a base work, an essential exercise allowing the artist to delve into form and movement to apply it in future projects.

The creation process was meticulous, taking advantage of clay's properties to model general forms and then carve fine details when the material reached the precise humidity point. This method allows the work to faithfully transmit the muscular tension and inner struggle that motivated the artist. Through this piece, the artist invites us to reflect on how even the simplest gestures, those we make daily, are a reflection of our interaction with the environment and the emotional load we carry inside.

Mitad.title: Fragmentado: Meditation on Resilience
Mitad.description: A meditation on resilience, where fractures and scars become part of the story, giving dignity and strength.
Mitad.history:
The conception of Fragmented is born from a personal experience of adversity. What was originally an anatomical study project was damaged by an accident, an event that, far from being the end of the work, became its turning point. The artist, inspired by the idea that one can rebuild completely after a catastrophe and that wounds' marks become part of personal history, decided to give a new meaning to the piece.

The work is a re-conceptualization of his already deep anatomical study. However, the fracture of the original sculpture allowed him to explore human antinomy from a more intimate and emotional perspective. The artist used clay and ceramic to create a game of textures and finishes, where meticulous carving of muscles and bones contrasts with the fragility of broken pieces. The tear is the key element humanizing the process; it symbolizes the pain necessary to accept one's own fragmentation. In this way, Fragmented is not only a work about reconstruction, but a reflection on how scars forge us, give us history and, ultimately, make us stronger.
Mitad.materials: Polychrome clay and ceramic sculpture (15 cm tall)

Davincci.title: Leonardo: Intellect and Temperance in Miniature
Davincci.description: A monument to the intellect and temperance of Leonardo da Vinci in an intimate format of only 7 cm.
Davincci.history:
At the heart of this piece lies the admiration for the tireless versatility of Leonardo da Vinci. The artist was driven to sculpt his figure not only for his renown, but for his bold curiosity to explore from the simplest facts of nature to the most complex works of art. The main challenge was to achieve harmony in every element of the face, seeking for the sum of its parts to reveal an expression of temperance and wisdom, the same that allowed da Vinci to defend his ideas and investigations against strong criticisms of his time.

The technique employed is a dual journey: an initial modeling to define general volumes, followed by meticulous carving in clay revealing the finest details. This artisanal process connects the artist with the same spirit of da Vinci, that of a creator who molds and perfects his vision. By opting for a small format, designed for a desk or library, the sculpture seeks to be a constant reminder of the legacy of this genius. It is a purely figurative work, stripped of external symbolisms to concentrate solely on the strength of facial features, a reminder that a man's true influence can reside in the power of his intellect and the depth of his gaze.
